headline: BTC.b token catalogued on Avalanche; multi-chain bridge with Security Consortium governance and audited contracts
short_headline: BTC.b discovered on Avalanche, Ethereum, Solana

findings.text: Avalanche C-Chain: BTC.b token (0x152b9d0FdC40C096757F570A51E494bd4b943E50) surfaced via Snowtrace block explorer; ERC-20 with 8 decimals, ~2,670 in circulation, 163k+ holders.
Deployments doc at docs.lombard.finance/use/bridging confirms BTC.b live on Avalanche (native), Ethereum (native), and Solana (native); LBTC available on 20+ chains via Chainlink CCIP.
Three independent audits confirmed by Avalanche blog and Lombard docs: OpenZeppelin (Dec 2024), Veridise (Aug 2024), and Halborn (Aug/Oct 2024); audit reports publicly available on GitHub.
No GitHub deployment artifacts located (GitHub fetch blocked); audits referenced as publicly available but direct fetch of GitHub audit folder failed.
BTC.b deployed on 3 chains: Avalanche C-Chain (primary, inherited from prior Ava Labs bridge), Ethereum (post-acquisition via Lombard), Solana (post-acquisition via Lombard).
No factory patterns identified; BTC.b is a single token contract bridged across chains via burn-and-mint model.

Security Consortium identified as 15-member institutional multisig (actor_class: multisig); listed members include OKX, Galaxy, DCG, Wintermute, Figment, Kiln, Antpool, F2Pool, Kraken, Amber; roles: validator, consensus participant.

rationale.verdict: Discovery catalogued: 1 token contract (BTC.b) across 3 chains, 1 institutional multisig (15-member Security Consortium), and 3 auditing firms. No GitHub repo addresses or off-chain admin/proxy addresses recovered due to fetch restrictions. Chainlink CCIP and Cubist Bascule identified as bridge infrastructure. Bug bounty via Immunefi ($250K limit) and security contact via discord/intercom noted in docs.

evidence.shows: BTC.b ERC-20 token on Avalanche C-Chain (chainId 43114), contract address 0x152b9d0FdC40C096757F570A51E494bd4b943E50, 8 decimals, ~2,670 circulating supply, 163k holders

BTC.b availability on Ethereum (native), Avalanche (native), and Solana (native); LBTC on 20+ chains via Chainlink CCIP; burn-and-mint bridging with dual-layer verification (CCIP + Symbiotic guarantee layer); Security Consortium approval required per bridge tx

BTC.b acquisition by Lombard from Ava Labs (Oct 2025); transition from Intel SGX (Warden) to Lombard's 15-member Security Consortium with BFT consensus; audit firms: OpenZeppelin, Veridise, Halborn (publicly available on GitHub); multi-chain expansion to Ethereum, Katana, MegaETH, Solana; Cubist CubeSigner HSM key management; Chainlink CCIP cross-chain messaging; contract address unchanged (0x152b9d0FdC40C096757F570A51E494bd4b943E50)

BTC.b is non-yield bridged Bitcoin asset; multi-chain operation on Avalanche, Ethereum, Solana, Katana, MegaETH; Security Consortium of 15 institutions (OKX, Galaxy, DCG, Wintermute, Figment, Kiln, Antpool, F2Pool, Kraken, Amber, and others); Hardware Security Module (HSM) via Cubist CubeSigner; dual verification via Bascule Drawbridge and Chainlink CCIP; permissionless minting, no KYC

Security architecture audited by OpenZeppelin, Veridise, and Halborn (audits publicly available on Github); Security Consortium validation on Lombard Ledger (BFT consensus); CubeSigner key management; Cubist Bascule Drawbridge and Chainlink CCIP dual-layer verification; Immunefi bug bounty program with $250K limit; 24/7 monitoring via Hexagate

protocol_metadata.about: <cite index="2-1">BTC.b is a next-generation Bitcoin asset, enabling holders to access onchain markets</cite>. <cite index="4-1">Lombard has acquired the infrastructure and related assets of BTC.b, and the Lombard Protocol will assume responsibility for BTC.b's bridge operations and security architecture</cite>. <cite index="5-17,5-18">Unlike existing wrapped Bitcoin products that rely on centralized custodians, BTC.b operates on Lombard's transparent, verifiable protocol architecture with every BTC.b token backed by native Bitcoin held in a decentralized security framework, verified through multiple independent layers including Chainlink Proof of Reserve and a consortium of 15 leading digital asset institutions</cite>.
